title: Trump meets Putin and Xi separately in Shenzhen as first three-way summit nears
dek: The Kremlin says Ukraine dominated a 40-minute Trump-Putin meeting; after an hour with Xi, Trump said they agreed oil must flow through Hormuz. No agreements were announced before the trilateral.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
US President Donald Trump held separate talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on Thursday, setting up the first face-to-face meeting of the leaders of the three powers later in the day. The Kremlin said Ukraine was the main subject of Trump's roughly 40-minute meeting with Putin. After about an hour with Xi, Trump said the two had agreed that oil should keep flowing through the Strait of Hormuz and that Iran could not have a nuclear weapon, according to reports.

Neither meeting produced an announced agreement. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said no particularly important statements had been made in the Putin meeting, and by early afternoon IST neither the White House nor China's foreign ministry had issued a readout of the Trump-Xi talks. There were no reports by early afternoon IST that the three-way meeting, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, had begun. Ukraine struck the bridge from Russia to Crimea again overnight, its third attack on the crossing this week.

## Thursday's meetings

Trump and Putin met at about 10.10 am IST at the Kylin Villa, a lakeside state guesthouse in north-west Shenzhen, in their first meeting since August 2025, according to reports. Trump told reporters the two had a long relationship and that "a lot of wonderful things can come out of this or at least start". Putin made no remarks in the part of the meeting open to the press. Ushakov told reporters afterwards that Ukraine had been the main topic and that Putin's mood was "great". Trump later said the meeting had "set the stage" for the three-way talks and that he hoped "something will come out" on the war in Ukraine, reports said.

Trump's meeting with Xi began shortly after 11 am IST and ended a little over an hour later, according to Chinese state television. Trump credited the US-China "Board of Trade" set up this year with balancing the relationship, said tariffs had been divided fairly, and said he would ask China to do more for American farmers, according to reports. He said the two countries could help end the Russia-Ukraine war. "You're my friend, and we have a very special relationship," he told Xi. Xi described relations as stable and improving and told Trump, "I remain committed to working with you," reports said.

Earlier, at the APEC leaders' plenary, Trump said he looked forward to "a historic trilateral meeting with President Xi and President Putin later today" and rejected what he called "globalist regulation" of frontier artificial intelligence, according to reports. In his own remarks to the leaders' meeting, published by China's foreign ministry, Xi called for keeping "industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded", for progress towards a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, and for "the broad application of AI". He said China would give $20 million to APEC cooperation projects and set up a Centre for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen.

The Kremlin had said the trilateral would last about an hour, but Ushakov said the leaders would decide its length themselves. Trump has pushed for nuclear arms control to be on the agenda, though Russia and China have shown little interest, according to reports. North Korean leader Kim Jong Un signalled that he would not meet Trump in China, reports said.

## On Wednesday

Trump flew in on Wednesday from Manila, where he had held the first Quad summit since 2024 with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the leaders of Japan and Australia, and was met on the tarmac by Xi. Xi told him at a welcome banquet that he wanted to "advance a constructive, strategic and stable relationship", according to Chinese state media reports. Earlier, opening the APEC CEO Summit, Xi said "unilateralism and protectionism are rampant" and that China's economy had grown 4.6 per cent in the first three quarters of the year, according to China's foreign ministry.

Xi also met Putin for about two hours on Wednesday, their fifth meeting this year, and said the two countries "must firmly shoulder the responsibilities expected of major powers", according to the Chinese readout.

## Background

The Shenzhen meeting was first confirmed by Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on 14 November. The Kremlin has dismissed comparisons with the 1945 Yalta conference as "games of political scientists", while Beijing has described the meeting as of "groundbreaking significance", reports said.

Trump visited China for a summit with Xi in May, and Putin travelled to Beijing days later. Thursday's was Trump and Xi's third meeting in person this year.

The meeting comes as relations over technology have sharpened again. On 16 November the US Commerce Department issued a rule requiring licences to send advanced AI chips to data centres in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil that serve Chinese customers. China's foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Tuesday that the rule overstretched the concept of national security and amounted to economic coercion, and that "China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate rights and interests". A day later Nvidia said it had removed about $2.4 billion a quarter of H200 chip sales to China from its forecast, according to reports.

The US and Iran have been at war since joint US-Israeli strikes in February, and fighting around the Strait of Hormuz flared again this week, with US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island and Iranian drone attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait.

## Why it matters for India

India is not a member of APEC and has no seat at Thursday's table, but most of the issues on it bear directly on Indian interests. The war with Iran has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a route for a large share of India's oil and gas imports, and Indian seafarers have been caught in the attacks: one Indian crew member of the LPG tanker Tara Gas has been missing since Monday, the Ministry of External Affairs said this week. Any understanding on Ukraine would affect India's large purchases of Russian oil, and the state of US-China trade talks shapes the tariffs and export controls that Indian manufacturers depend on for electronics components, solar equipment and rare earths.

At the Quad summit in Manila on Tuesday, Modi, Trump and the leaders of Japan and Australia warned against economic coercion and "arbitrary export restrictions" without naming any country. Wednesday's scenes in Shenzhen showed the same US president seeking a working relationship with Beijing and Moscow a day later. India's Ministry of External Affairs had not commented on the Shenzhen meetings by Thursday afternoon.

## What happens next

The three-way meeting is due later on Thursday. China's foreign ministry has said it will release information "in a timely manner", and the Kremlin and White House are expected to give their own accounts. The US-China trade truce agreed earlier this year expires on 10 January, and Trump and Xi are expected to meet again at the G20 summit in Miami in December, according to reports. APEC leaders end their meeting on Thursday. The Declaration will update this story when the leaders' talks end.

## Key numbers

- 3: leaders at the first-ever US-China-Russia summit, due on 19 November
- About 40 minutes: Trump's meeting with Putin; about an hour with Xi
- 4.6%: China's growth in the first three quarters, according to Xi
- $2.4 billion: Nvidia's H200 sales to China last quarter, now excluded from its forecast
- 21: APEC member economies; India is not one of them
